findings.summary: The cost section should say where the per-call price comes from, and that a running check records the real cost from Jev's responses.
findings.evidence: defaults-loop.md section 6: 'Cost and tokens are read from the response and stored; they are never estimated by the client. (The cost figure in the probe report was garbled, so no per-call cost is taken from it here.)' The plan uses $0.00001 from the request but does not mention this conflict. Fix: In the cost section, label $0.00001 as the request's stated figure, not a measured one. Note that defaults-loop.md section 6 has no measured price. Have the shadow record format (J1) store the cost and tokens each response reports, so the shadow period gives a measured cost per landing.
findings.location: Plan decision 5 (cost per landing); docs/design/defaults-loop.md lines 317-318

findings.summary: Scoring measures precision only. Nothing counts files Jev did not flag that later break or churn, so the exit rule cannot tell a cautious Jev from a useful one.
findings.evidence: Decision 4 defines a hit for a flagged file and for a recommended split, and an exit rule of 'precision above the baseline'. There is no measure for misses, and churn above the median also counts as a hit, so Jev can score well just by flagging files that already churn a lot. Fix: Add a recall or miss measure to the scoring section: unflagged changed files that later break or churn. Require the exit rule to beat the baseline on precision with recall no worse than the baseline. Also state that the churn window starts after the flagged landing, so a file is not scored on churn that came before the flag.

findings.summary: The plan does not say what happens when the top option is the neutral 'none' (or 'one thing') option with a high p_top.
findings.evidence: defaults-loop.md section 6.1 explains why p_top misleads for booleans (a confident 'false' is still a high p_top). The same trap applies to a choice question whose top answer is the neutral option. Fix: For each question, say which option or options are 'flag' options, and compare the threshold with the probability of the chosen flag option (or the sum of the flag options' probabilities). A confident neutral answer then always means nothing happens.
findings.location: Plan decision 1 (thresholds on p_top with a none option)

summary: The plan meets the request and the accepted reading. I checked its key claims against the snapshot and they hold. docs/design/hestia.md, scope-guard.md and defaults-loop.md all exist. defaults-loop.md has sections 6, 6.1 (p_top is the threshold input for choice questions but not for booleans) and 6.2 (escalation). docs/decisions.md ends at D129, which is marked proposed, and D127 is the scope guard. D90 and D92 put Jev in shadow with code deciding. crates/athena-cli/src/decisions.rs pins PINNED_LEN 230046 and has the_decision_log_is_well_formed_and_only_appended_to. backtest.rs PHRASES holds exactly 'superseded by', 'supersedes' and 'amends', so appending D130 without them leaves decision-links.toml unchanged. The five questions, the per-unit bounded state, the graded effects (structural pass only with a deterministic trip or after shadow exit), scoring by landing records against a deterministic baseline, the labeled cost arithmetic and the six-job build plan cover criteria 1 to 5. For content-only criteria, reading the diff is a fair demonstration, and cargo test --locked covers criterion 6. I found three minor points: the per-call price conflicts with what defaults-loop.md says about cost, the scoring measures precision only, and the plan does not say what happens when 'none' is the top option.
